page_title: Trello tribute with Phoenix and React (pt.1)

summary.title: Trello tribute with Phoenix and React (pt.1)
summary.one_liner: Learn the planned stack and scope for building a Trello-style app with Elixir, Phoenix, React, Redux and real-time channels, as the first part of a series.
takeaways: The app is a single-page Trello-style board tool with sign up, sign in, boards, member sharing, lists and cards.
The back-end uses Elixir, Phoenix, Ecto and PostgreSQL; the front-end uses Webpack, Sass, React, React Router, Redux and ES6/ES7.
Phoenix channels (websockets) provide real-time updates and connected-user tracking without extra dependencies, according to the author.
The series is outlined in 11 parts, from project setup and JWT auth to sockets, boards, lists and Heroku deployment.
summary.summary: This is the intro post of a multi-part series that builds a simplified Trello clone. It explains the goal: users sign in, create boards, share them with other users, and add lists and cards, with changes pushed to connected browsers in real time. The post justifies the stack, covering Elixir and Phoenix for the back-end with Phoenix's built-in websockets, and React, React Router and Redux for the single-page front-end. It ends by previewing part 2, which covers project setup and switching from Brunch to Webpack.
